# Introduction

BIGpopA is an R package for pedigree quality control, parentage assignment and breed/line composition from SNP genotypes. It works for diploid and polyploid species and is the analytical engine behind the [Familia](https://github.com/Breeding-Insight/Familia) Shiny app. This guide runs the functions in the order a breeding program usually needs them:

1. Convert genotypes to the dosage table used by every function. -> `vcf_to_dosage()`, `ped_to_dosage()`
2. Is the pedigree record clean? -> `check_ped()`
3. Do the recorded parents agree with the genotypes? -> `validate_pedigree()`
4. Who are the parents of an individual with unknown or wrong parents? -> `find_parentage()`
5. What is the line / breed composition of each sample? -> `allele_freq_poly()`, `solve_composition_poly()`, `assign_composition_line()`

| Function | Use it to | Main output |
|---|---|---|
| `vcf_to_dosage()` | Convert a VCF to allele-B dosages | Dosage table or matrix |
| `ped_to_dosage()` | Convert a PLINK `.ped` (diploid) to allele-B dosages | Dosage table or matrix |
| `check_ped()` | Fix structural pedigree errors before any genotype work | Corrected pedigree, issue tables |
| `validate_pedigree()` | Test recorded trios against genotypes | Status per trio, corrected pedigree, marker summary |
| `find_parentage()` | Assign or fill in parents from a candidate pool | Best parent(s), error %, ties |
| `allele_freq_poly()` | Allele frequencies of reference lines | Frequency table (markers x lines) |
| `solve_composition_poly()` | Composition of samples from reference frequencies | Proportions and R2 per sample |
| `assign_composition_line()` | Percentages and assigned line per sample | Composition table |

Remarks on the data (violations give misleading results):

- **Genotypes are allele-B dosages** (0 to ploidy), not allele pairs. Convert VCF or PLINK files with the two converters below.
- **Ploidy is correct.** The Mendelian rules depend on the gametes each parent can produce (ploidy / 2 alleles). A wrong ploidy produces many false failures, so set it to the ploidy of your dosages. Even ploidies use a polysomic gamete-range test (assumes autopolyploid inheritance, so it is conservative for allopolyploids). Odd ploidies (e.g. triploid) fall back to an opposite-homozygote test on homozygous markers only, which has less power.
- **Offspring come from normal sexual reproduction.** Selfed, inbred, doubled-haploid or clonal material can break the assumptions of the trio test (see the Tips section).
- **Marker names and individual ids match exactly** between files (case and spaces matter).

BIGpopA does not call dosages; use your pipeline first (we recommend [BIGapp](https://github.com/Breeding-Insight/BIGapp)).

# Install

BIGpopA requires R >= 4.4.0. Install it from CRAN by copying and pasting this code into your R console:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("BIGpopA")
library(BIGpopA)
```

# Input data

Every function accepts either a file path or an in-memory object (data.frame / data.table). `founders_file` accepts a file path, a character vector of ids, or a data.frame whose first column holds the ids. This guide builds a small toy dataset that exercises every result category.

| Object | Format | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Pedigree | `id`, `male_parent`, `female_parent`. Unknown parent = `0`. | `check_ped()`, `validate_pedigree()` |
| Genotypes | `id` + one column per marker (allele-B dosage, `NA` = missing) | `validate_pedigree()`, `find_parentage()` |
| Parents | `id` and `sex` (`M`, `F`, `A` = either). Without a `sex` column all candidates are treated as `A`. | `find_parentage()` |
| Progeny | `id` column. For *fill_pedigree*: the 3-column pedigree (unknown parent = `0`, `NA` or empty). | `find_parentage()` |
| Founders | File path, character vector or data.frame (first column) | `validate_pedigree()`, `find_parentage()` |

```{r}
library(BIGpopA)

# SNP genotypes coded 0/1/2 (NA = missing); C_low is mostly missing
genotypes = data.frame(
  id    = c("M1","F1","M2","F2","C1","C2","C3","C_bad","C_low"),
  snp01 = c(  0,   0,   2,   2,   0,   2,   1,     0,     NA),
  snp02 = c(  0,   0,   2,   0,   0,   1,   0,     0,     NA),
  snp03 = c(  0,   2,   0,   2,   1,   1,   1,     1,     NA),
  snp04 = c(  0,   2,   0,   0,   1,   0,   0,     1,     NA),
  snp05 = c(  2,   0,   1,   1,   1,   1,   1,     1,     NA),
  snp06 = c(  2,   0,   1,   0,   1,   1,   1,     1,     NA),
  snp07 = c(  2,   2,   0,   1,   2,   0,   2,     2,     NA),
  snp08 = c(  2,   2,   2,   2,   2,   2,   2,     2,     NA),
  snp09 = c(  0,   1,   0,   2,   1,   1,   1,     1,      0),
  snp10 = c(  0,   1,   2,   0,   0,   1,   0,     0,      0),
  snp11 = c(  2,   1,   1,   2,   1,   2,   2,     1,      2),
  snp12 = c(  2,   1,   0,   1,   2,   1,   1,     2,      2),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# pedigree with founders coded 0, a mis-assigned trio (C_bad),
# and a duplicated row (C_missing)
pedigree = data.frame(
  id            = c("M1","F1","M2","F2","C1","C2","C3","C_bad","C_low","C_missing","C_missing"),
  male_parent   = c("0", "0", "0", "0", "M1","M2","M1","M2",   "M1",   "M1",       "M1"),
  female_parent = c("0", "0", "0", "0", "F1","F2","F2","F1",   "F1",   "F1",       "F1"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# candidate parents (with sex) and progeny to assign
parents = data.frame(
  id  = c("M1","M2","F1","F2"),
  sex = c("M", "M", "F", "F"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

progeny = data.frame(id = c("C1","C2","C3","C_bad","C_low","C_missing"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

pedigree
```

The pedigree has four founders (`M1`, `F1`, `M2`, `F2`, both parents `0`) and several crosses, including a duplicated row (`C_missing`), a mis-assigned trio (`C_bad`) and a sample with mostly missing genotypes (`C_low`).

## Converting genotype files

Use these converters when your genotypes come as a VCF or a PLINK file. Both return an `id` column followed by one column per marker, ready for `validate_pedigree()` and `find_parentage()`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# VCF (.vcf or .vcf.gz); ploidy is inferred from the GT field when NULL
geno_vcf = vcf_to_dosage("my_markers.vcf.gz", ploidy = 4)

# PLINK .ped (diploid only); a .map file next to it is used for marker names
geno_ped = ped_to_dosage("my_markers.ped")

# format = "matrix" returns individuals x markers, the input of
# allele_freq_poly() and solve_composition_poly()
geno_mat = vcf_to_dosage("my_markers.vcf.gz", ploidy = 4, format = "matrix")
```

Useful `vcf_to_dosage()` arguments:

| Argument | Effect |
|---|---|
| `ploidy` | Checked against the ploidy observed in the file; a warning is issued if they disagree |
| `dosage_field` | Read a FORMAT field with dosages (e.g. `"DS"`, `"UD"`) instead of counting alleles in `GT`; `ploidy` must be given |
| `ref_dosage` | Count reference instead of alternate alleles (default `FALSE`) |
| `biallelic_only` | Drop markers with more than one ALT allele (default `TRUE`) |
| `min_marker_call_rate`, `min_sample_call_rate` | Drop markers / individuals with a lower call rate (default 0 = no filtering) |

# Pedigree cleaning

`check_ped()` works on the columns `id`, `male_parent` and `female_parent`. It applies the checks in this order:

| Issue | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Exact duplicates | The identical row appears more than once | Always removed |
| Conflicting trios | Same `id`, different parents in different rows | Disagreeing parents set to `0` and rows collapsed, or flagged (`correct_conflicting_trios = FALSE`) |
| Missing parents | A parent is listed but has no row of its own | Always added as a row with unknown parents (`0`) |
| Inconsistent sex roles | Same individual used as sire and as dam | Set to `0` as a parent everywhere, or flagged (`correct_inconsistent_sex_roles = FALSE`) |
| Cycles / dependencies | An individual is its own ancestor, or is recorded as its own parent | Flagged only; must be fixed manually, since there is no safe automatic choice |

Unknown parents must be coded `0`.

```{r}
clean_ped_results = check_ped(pedigree, verbose = FALSE)

# the corrected, analysis-ready pedigree
clean_ped = clean_ped_results$corrected_pedigree
clean_ped
```

The result also holds one table per issue, for example `clean_ped_results$exact_duplicates` (here the repeated `C_missing` row) and `clean_ped_results$missing_parents`. An empty table means the issue was not found. Set `verbose = TRUE` to print a full report to the console.

# Pedigree validation

`validate_pedigree()` compares every trio (offspring, male parent, female parent) with the genotypes and computes a Mendelian error rate. A marker is *testable* when the offspring and both parents have a call.

```{r}
ped_validate_results = validate_pedigree(clean_ped, genotypes,
                                         verbose = FALSE, plot_results = TRUE)

ped_validate_report = ped_validate_results$full_results
ped_validate_report
```

## Parameters

| Argument | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ploidy` | 2 | Ploidy of the dosages |
| `trio_error_threshold` | 5 | Maximum % of testable markers with a Mendelian error for a trio to *pass* |
| `min_markers` | 10 | Minimum testable markers needed to judge a trio; fewer gives `low_markers` |
| `single_parent_error_threshold` | 2 | Maximum homozygous mismatch % for a single parent to pass the single-parent check |
| `founders_file` | `NULL` | File path, vector of ids or data.frame; ids listed here with both parents `0` are reported as `founders` |
| `marker_trio_table` | `FALSE` | Also return the marker x trio table (see below) |
| `plot_results` | `TRUE` | Draw a histogram of trio error percentages |

## Status of each trio

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pass` | Mendelian error at or below `trio_error_threshold` |
| `fail` | Error above the threshold |
| `low_markers` | Fewer than `min_markers` testable markers |
| `no_genotype_data` | At least one of the three individuals is not in the genotype file |
| `founders` | Both parents `0` and the id is in `founders_file` |
| `missing_both_parents`, `missing_male_parent`, `missing_female_parent` | One or both parents are `0` |
| `no_data` | No testable marker at all |

In the toy data `C1`, `C2` and `C3` pass, `C_bad` fails, `C_low` is `low_markers` and `C_missing` has `no_genotype_data`.

## Failed trios and recommended correction

For a failed trio the function checks each parent alone, using only markers where the parent and the offspring are both homozygous (an offspring homozygous for one allele cannot have a parent homozygous for the other). The `recommended_correction` column gives the result:

| `recommended_correction` | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| `none` | Trio passes, or it is a founder, has a missing parent, has no genotype data or has no testable marker |
| `remove_male_parent` | The trio fails and only the male parent fails the single-parent check |
| `remove_female_parent` | The trio fails and only the female parent fails the single-parent check |
| `remove_both` | The trio fails and both parents fail the single-parent check |
| `unresolved` | The trio fails but neither parent fails the single-parent check, for example an offspring recorded as its own parent; the pedigree is probably wrong but the faulty parent cannot be identified |
| `low_markers_*` | The trio has fewer than `min_markers` testable markers; the suffix is the decision the same rules would give (`low_markers_keep_both` means the error is within the threshold and both parents pass) |

```{r}
ped_validate_results$corrected_pedigree
```

`corrected_pedigree` sets the parent(s) named by the recommendation to `0`. Run `find_parentage()` with `method = "fill_pedigree"` afterwards to look for the right parent.

## Marker summary

`marker_summary` lists every marker with `trios_tested`, `trios_mismatch` and `mismatch_pct`, sorted worst first. It answers a different question than the trio table: *is the problem the individual or the marker?* A few markers with a mismatch % far above the rest (paralogous loci, poor clustering, null alleles) inflate the error of many trios. Remove them from the genotype file and rerun.

```{r}
head(ped_validate_results$marker_summary)
```

## Marker x trio table

Set `marker_trio_table = TRUE` to see, for each marker and each trio, where an error comes from. Columns are named `id_male_female`.

```{r}
mt_results = validate_pedigree(clean_ped, genotypes, verbose = FALSE,
                               plot_results = FALSE, marker_trio_table = TRUE)
mt_results$marker_trio_table
```

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `match` | The trio is consistent at this marker |
| `mismatch_male`, `mismatch_female` | Only that parent is inconsistent with the offspring |
| `mismatch_both` | Each parent alone is inconsistent with the offspring |
| `mismatch_combination` | Each parent alone is compatible, but the pair cannot produce the offspring |
| `missing_male`, `missing_female`, `missing_progeny` | That individual has no call; every missing individual is named (for example `missing_progeny_male_female`) |
| `untestable` | No call is missing, but the marker cannot be tested (odd ploidy, offspring not homozygous) |

# Missing data

Missing marker calls (`NA`) are handled marker by marker and never count as errors:

- **validate_pedigree().** A marker is *testable* for a trio only if the offspring and both parents have a call (odd ploidy: the offspring is homozygous and at least one parent has a call and is homozygous). The error % is mismatches / testable markers. Trios with fewer testable markers than `min_markers` are labeled `low_markers`; trios with none are `no_data` (only in `full_results`).
- **Single-parent check.** Uses only markers where both parent and offspring are homozygous. If there are none, the parent counts as failing.
- **Marker summary.** `mismatch_pct` is `NA` for markers not tested in any trio.
- **find_parentage().** Same testable-marker logic per candidate; a candidate with no testable markers gets `markers_tested = 0` and `low_markers`.
- **allele_freq_poly().** A marker missing in every reference individual of a line has no frequency; `solve_composition_poly()` stops with an error listing these markers. Remove them and rerun.

# Parentage assignment

When parentage is unknown, `find_parentage()` searches a pool of candidate parents for the best assignment to each progeny.

```{r}
find_parentage_results = find_parentage(genotypes, parents, progeny,
                                        method = "best_pair",
                                        verbose = FALSE, plot_results = TRUE)

find_parentage_report = find_parentage_results$full_results
find_parentage_report
```

## Parameters

| Argument | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `"best_pair"` | The search (see below) |
| `ploidy` | 2 | Ploidy of the dosages |
| `error_threshold` | 5 | Error % above which the best candidate gets `high_error` |
| `min_markers` | 10 | If the best candidate has fewer testable markers, the status is `low_markers` |
| `top_n` | 1 | Report the best `top_n` candidates per progeny |
| `show_ties` | `TRUE` | Report `tied_candidates` |
| `allow_parent_selfing` | `FALSE` | Allow the same individual as male and female parent |
| `exclude_self_match` | `TRUE` | Do not let a progeny match itself as parent |
| `founders_file` | `NULL` | File path, vector of ids or data.frame; founders are skipped by `fill_pedigree` |

| Method | Searches |
|---|---|
| `best_pair` | Male x female pair with the lowest Mendelian error (needs both sexes in the parents table) |
| `best_male_parent`, `best_female_parent` | The single candidate of that sex with the lowest homozygous mismatch (compares only markers homozygous in both candidate and offspring); use when the other parent is known or unavailable |
| `best_match` | Same homozygous mismatch test over candidates of either sex |
| `fill_pedigree` | Missing parents of a 3-column pedigree (see below) |

The best candidate is always reported. The status is `pass` (error at or below `error_threshold`), `high_error` (above it, so treat the assignment with caution), `low_markers`, or `known_parent_no_genotype`. In the toy data `C_bad`, which failed validation, is recovered to its true pair (`M1`/`F1`) at 0% error, while `C_low` remains `low_markers`.

## Top N and ties

`tied_candidates` is the number of candidates (pairs for `best_pair`) that share the lowest error of a progeny; values above 1 mean the best assignment is ambiguous. This is common with few markers or with clones. With `top_n > 1`, rank 1 stays in the base columns and ranks 2 to `top_n` are added as suffix columns (`male_parent_2`, `female_parent_2`, `mendelian_error_pct_2`).

```{r}
find_parentage(genotypes, parents, progeny, method = "best_pair", top_n = 3,
               verbose = FALSE, plot_results = FALSE)$full_results
```

## Filling in missing parents of a pedigree

With `method = "fill_pedigree"`, `progeny` is a pedigree with `id`, `male_parent` and `female_parent` (for example `validate_pedigree()$corrected_pedigree`). Parents coded `0`, `NA` or empty are unknown. A known male parent searches only females, a known female parent only males, and rows with both unknown get the full pair search; rows with both parents known are skipped. The parents table (with sex `M`, `F` or `A`) is still required. The output adds `search_mode` and `known_parent_error_pct`.

```{r}
ped_to_fill = data.frame(id = c("C1", "C2"),
                         male_parent = c("M1", "0"),
                         female_parent = c("0", "0"))

find_parentage(genotypes, parents, ped_to_fill, method = "fill_pedigree",
               verbose = FALSE, plot_results = FALSE)$full_results
```

# Breed and line composition

BIGpopA estimates genome-wide breed or line composition for diploid and polyploid populations with a breedTools-style quadratic programming approach (Funkhouser et al. 2017). The workflow has three steps: compute reference-line allele frequencies, estimate the composition of each sample, and assign each sample to a line. This example mirrors an autotetraploid analysis (`ploidy = 4`) that assigns samples to two cultivar reference panels, Jewel and Draper.

```{r}
# reference genotypes: individuals x SNPs, tetraploid dosage of allele B (0..4)
reference = data.frame(
  S1 = c(0, 1, 0, 4, 3, 4),
  S2 = c(1, 0, 0, 3, 4, 4),
  S3 = c(0, 1, 1, 4, 3, 3),
  S4 = c(1, 0, 1, 3, 4, 3),
  S5 = c(0, 1, 0, 4, 3, 4),
  S6 = c(1, 0, 1, 3, 4, 3),
  row.names = c("Jewel1","Jewel2","Jewel3","Draper1","Draper2","Draper3")
)

# reference panel membership (which individuals define each cultivar)
ref_ids = list(
  Jewel  = c("Jewel1","Jewel2","Jewel3"),
  Draper = c("Draper1","Draper2","Draper3")
)

# allele frequencies of the reference panels (SNPs x panels)
freq = allele_freq_poly(reference, ref_ids, ploidy = 4)
freq
```

The references should be representative, unadmixed individuals; the more distinct the references, the better the estimate. Marker names must match between the reference and the samples.

```{r}
# samples to assign: samples x SNPs (same SNPs as the reference)
validation = data.frame(
  S1 = c(0, 4, 2),
  S2 = c(1, 3, 2),
  S3 = c(0, 4, 2),
  S4 = c(1, 3, 2),
  S5 = c(0, 4, 2),
  S6 = c(1, 3, 2),
  row.names = c("Sample1","Sample2","Sample3")
)

# composition (one column per panel plus an R2 model-fit column)
prediction = as.data.frame(solve_composition_poly(validation, freq, ploidy = 4))
prediction
```

The model returns an R2 value, but it is expected to be low because a discrete allele dosage is regressed on a continuous allele frequency.

`assign_composition_line()` turns the result into the table used by Familia: the estimated percentage of each panel and a `Predicted line`. A sample is assigned to its highest-proportion line only if that proportion is at least `assign_threshold` (default 50); otherwise it is labelled `Undetermined`. With `assign_threshold = 0` every sample is assigned.

```{r}
pred_results = assign_composition_line(solve_composition_poly(validation, freq, ploidy = 4))
pred_results
```

`Sample1` is assigned Jewel and `Sample2` Draper (each essentially 100%), while the admixed `Sample3` splits roughly evenly between them. For diploid data set `ploidy = 2`. Save the table with `write.table(pred_results, "composition.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE)`.

# Complete workflow

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# genotypes
genotypes = vcf_to_dosage("my_markers.vcf.gz", ploidy = 4)

# pedigree quality control
clean_ped = check_ped(pedigree)$corrected_pedigree
validated = validate_pedigree(clean_ped, genotypes, ploidy = 4)
assigned  = find_parentage(genotypes, parents, progeny, method = "fill_pedigree",
                           ploidy = 4)

# breed/line composition
freq       = allele_freq_poly(reference, ref_ids, ploidy = 4)
prediction = solve_composition_poly(validation, freq, ploidy = 4)
composition_table = assign_composition_line(prediction, assign_threshold = 50)
```

# Tips

- Typical workflow: `check_ped()` -> `validate_pedigree()` -> `find_parentage()` (`fill_pedigree`) on the corrected pedigree.
- Make sure you are using the right ploidy. A wrong ploidy gives many false failures.
- Selfed or inbred offspring can fail the trio test; check the single-parent errors and the `unresolved` flag.
- Ties are common with few markers or with clones; always check `tied_candidates`.
- Check `marker_summary` before blaming individuals; remove bad markers and rerun.
